Overview

This report compiles 379 publicly announced data center deals dated Jan 1, 2025 through Oct 12, 2026: new builds, expansions, leases, acquisitions, financings and project-tied power agreements. Across the deals that stated figures, announcements total 129,943.4 MW of capacity and $2.1T in U.S.-dollar value. Every number, date, deal type, place and company name in this report is a link: numbers open a panel listing the exact deals behind them, and each deal links to its full entry, its company profiles and its numbered sources.

Method

Publicly announced deals only. MW and dollar figures appear only where a source stated them; a dash means the source gave none. Deals stated in other currencies (ringgit, euros, Singapore dollars and so on) carry no USD value and are left out of the dollar totals—there is no currency conversion. A few announcement dates are approximate per source reporting; the deal notes say so where that applies. Same-party transactions close together were kept separate where sources describe distinct deals. Totals add up stated figures and may double-count where, for example, a financing funds a build that is also listed. Company links are matched on company names in each deal’s text, so a profile’s “named in” list covers counterparties, lenders, tenants and other mentions.

By state

180 of the 379 deals name at least one U.S. state, spread across 36 states (counting D.C.). The states with the most deals are Texas (47), Georgia (12), North Dakota (12), Pennsylvania (12), Virginia (11). Another 30 deals are in the U.S. but name no state (typically company-wide financings or multi-site leases), 125 are outside the U.S., and 44 list no specific place. Hover a state for its numbers; click it for its deals.

Shade by:
 

A deal that names more than one state (8 deals) counts once toward each state’s deal count, but its MW and dollar figures are left out of the state totals because the sources don’t say how they split. Deal counts are shaded in fixed steps (1, 2–3, 4–6, 7–11, 12+); MW and value are shaded in five equal-size groups of the states that stated figures. Pale gray means none.

ThisWay Global Inc. #

Oct 12, 2026 · New build · Bryan, TX · 73 MW

ThisWay Global announced plans for the Research and AI Compute Center (RACC) at the Texas A&M-RELLIS campus in Bryan: a phased 73 MW sovereign AI/HPC development on a 25-acre site for research, public-sector and industry users, following the company's Sept. 30, 2026 court-approved acquisition of the previously stalled project's assets for $40M through the bankruptcy process. [1]

Undisclosed developer #

Oct 12, 2026 · New build · Metter, GA

An anonymous developer (via Canoochee River RV Resort LLC) submitted a state application for a five-building data center campus in Metter, Candler County, Georgia (~250,000 sq ft per building, closed-loop cooling, two on-site substations), phased to complete by 2033. Early planning-stage filing; no MW figures or developer identity disclosed. [2]

Big Watt Digital / PowerHouse Data Centers (JV) #

Oct 9, 2026 · New build · Taylor, TX · 1,000 MW

The Big Watt Digital-PowerHouse Data Centers JV secured approval of its development agreement with the City of Taylor for the Taylor Technology Campus on a ~664-acre site in the Austin metro, designed to deliver up to 1 GW of hyperscale capacity with dedicated behind-the-meter gas generation; construction slated 2027-2029, initial power in H1 2028. This is a planning-approval milestone, not a tenant deal. [3]

Singtel #

Oct 9, 2026 · Financing · Tuas, Singapore · 58 MW · $476M

Singtel secured a S$643M (~$476M) five-year green loan from a DBS, OCBC, Standard Chartered, HSBC and UOB consortium to construct its 58MW DC Tuas AI-ready data center, operational in 2026. [4]

Note: Date inferred: article reported 'announced on Friday' and was crawled ~6 days before Oct 12, 2026, i.e. Oct 9. USD figure is the source's own conversion.

Bitdeer AI (Bitdeer Technologies Group) #

Oct 8, 2026 · Lease · Malaysia · 67 MW

Bitdeer AI entered a 10-year data center services agreement for A901, a 67 MW (critical IT load) AI Cloud campus in Malaysia, its third Malaysian hub alongside Cyberjaya and Johor, engineered for liquid-cooled NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks; first delivery targeted Q1 2027, full 67 MW by Q2 2027; site location and operator undisclosed. [5]

Green AI Cloud #

Oct 8, 2026 · Acquisition · Stockholm, Sweden · $300M · with Pioneer Acquisition I Corp (Nasdaq: PACH)

Stockholm-based AI infrastructure firm Green AI Cloud signed a definitive business combination with SPAC Pioneer Acquisition I Corp at a $300M pre-money equity value, to take the company public on Nasdaq (expected Q2 2027) and fund expansion of its renewable-powered European AI data centers. [6]

AirTrunk #

Oct 7, 2026 · Financing · Inzai, Japan · $1B · with SMBC, MUFG Bank, UOB (green loan leads)

Blackstone-backed AirTrunk secured a $1B green loan (led by SMBC, MUFG Bank and UOB) to invest in its 300+ MW TOK1 campus in Inzai to deploy liquid cooling for AI workloads, with first liquid-cooled capacity expected January 2028. [7]

CoreWeave #

Oct 7, 2026 · New build · Navi Mumbai, India · 240 MW · with AdaniConneX

CoreWeave announced its entry into India via a collaboration with AdaniConneX for 240 MW of AI data center capacity at AdaniConneX's Taloja campus in Navi Mumbai (three 80 MW buildings, CoreWeave as sole tenant, NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform), with an option to double capacity by another 240 MW; first phase targeted mid-2028. Some reports date the announcement Oct 8. [8]

Digital Realty (MC Digital Realty JV) #

Oct 7, 2026 · Expansion · Osaka, Japan · 24 MW

Digital Realty commenced construction of KIX15, a 24 MW data center at its KIX Campus in Ibaraki City, Osaka (fifth building on campus, developed by its 50/50 MC Digital Realty JV with Mitsubishi), scheduled to open Q4 2028 and bringing MCDR's Japan portfolio to 10 data centers and ~220 MW of aggregate IT capacity. [9]

Digital Realty #

Oct 6, 2026 · Financing · US

Digital Realty priced a €1B offering of 5.125% green Guaranteed Notes due 2036 via Digital Euro Finco, with proceeds allocable to its Green Bond Framework projects including energy efficiency and renewables across its data center platform. [10][11]

Note: Value stated as €1B only, not converted to USD. Corporate green bond, not tied to a single site.

Digital Realty #

Oct 6, 2026 · Financing · US

Digital Realty closed CHF510M of Swiss bonds in three tranches (2029/2032/2036) via Digital Constellation B.V., adding to its long-dated funding mix for global data center investment. [12]

Note: Value stated as CHF510M only, not converted to USD. Announced same day as the €1B green bond — separate transactions, no double count.

Google #

Oct 6, 2026 · Power · PJM grid (Illinois, Pennsylvania, New Jersey) · 890 MW · $4.3B · with Constellation Energy

Google signed a 20-year PPA with Constellation to add 890 MW of new nuclear capacity via uprates at 11 existing reactors across six sites in IL/PA/NJ (>$4.3B Constellation investment, first uprates 2028, full block by 2032), plus a separate 15-year energy supply agreement for 2,700 MW from Constellation's existing PJM fleet, driven by Google's data center growth. [13][14]

Macquarie Capital #

Oct 6, 2026 · Acquisition · Singapore · 2,000 MW · with Zerra DC

Singapore hyperscale developer Zerra DC secured an investment from Macquarie Capital (terms undisclosed) to expand its APAC hyperscale platform, including the Western Downs Digital Park in Queensland; Zerra's development pipeline exceeds 2 GW of planned IT capacity across Australia, Japan and India. Macquarie Capital took an undisclosed stake in Singapore-based hyperscale data center developer Zerra DC to support expansion across APAC. Zerra, majority-owned by AGP, has a development pipeline of more than 2 GW of planned IT capacity across Australia, Japan and India (including the Western Downs Digital Park in Queensland, which has a long-term lease commitment from Anthropic). Note: capacity is planned pipeline, not operating. [15][16]

atNorth #

Oct 5, 2026 · New build · Salo, Finland · 75 MW

atNorth announced FIN05, a new data center on a 28.6-hectare site in Salo with power secured for a 75 MW first phase and a path to 230 MW; the company estimates its investment at ~€2B (excluding customer-owned servers, up to ~€10B more). [17]

Sabey Corporation / National Real Estate Advisors #

Oct 5, 2026 · Acquisition · Seattle, WA · with Ares Secondaries funds

Ares Secondaries funds expanded their minority equity investment in Sabey Data Center Properties (follows July 2026 stake), bringing total Ares commitment above $500M; SDCP operates 275 MW of US hyperscale/enterprise campuses with a pipeline toward ~737 MW by 2033. [18]

Sinar Mas (SMPlus Digital Investama) #

Oct 5, 2026 · Acquisition · Jakarta, Indonesia · with Princeton Digital Group

Princeton Digital Group agreed to sell five operational Indonesian data centers (Jakarta, Bandung, Surabaya, Pekanbaru) to SMPlus Digital Investama (SM+), the digital infrastructure platform of Indonesian conglomerate Sinar Mas, as PDG narrows its Indonesian focus to a 400 MW hyperscale pipeline around Jakarta. Price and combined capacity were not disclosed. Note: announcement date inferred — agreement signed 'on Monday' per Mingtiandi reporting published ~Oct 11, 2026 (Monday = Oct 5, 2026). [19]

TeraWulf Inc. #

Oct 5, 2026 · Power · Grayson, KY · 1,000 MW · with Kentucky Power (AEP)

TeraWulf signed an amended electric service agreement with Kentucky Power doubling contracted power at its Muskie Data Campus in Grayson, Kentucky from 500 MW to 1 GW, accelerating the second 500 MW phase from 2030 to 2029; TeraWulf also agreed to fund $100M of residential winter bill credits and pay estimated financing costs for Kentucky Power's planned 760 MW Big Sandy combined-cycle plant. Subject to Kentucky PSC approval. [20]

Crusoe #

Oct 2, 2026 · New build · Jayton, TX · $4.8B

Crusoe filed TDLR plans for two data center buildings near Jayton in Kent County (~759k sq ft each, ~$2.4B each, $4.8B total), listed as 'spur buildings' of Project Hyper tied to its 1.4 GW Childress campus with Lancium; construction start Jan 2027, operations targeted May/July 2029. [21]

Lambda, Inc. #

Oct 1, 2026 · Financing · United States · $1B

Lambda closed a $1B investment-grade, delayed-draw senior secured term loan (fixed ~6.78%) to fund GPU infrastructure for three committed customer deployments with two investment-grade offtakers across multiple data centers; its first $1B+ institutional debt financing. [22]

Nscale #

Nscale raised $3.36B via pre-IPO convertible loan notes led by Third Point ($2.36B at closing plus a $1B NVIDIA commitment expected mid-November), with Apollo, Citadel and others participating, to accelerate global data center buildouts. [28][29]

Riot Platforms signed a 10-year, ~$311M wholesale data center lease with AMD for 25MW at its Rockdale, TX site. Note: AMD has an option to expand up to 200MW total; ~$1B value if all extensions exercised; Riot also acquired 200 acres at Rockdale for $96M the same day. [479][480]

STACK Infrastructure #

Jan 16, 2025 · New build · Stafford County, VA · 1,000 MW

STACK Infrastructure announced the 1+GW Stafford Technology Campus in Northern Virginia, a landmark hyperscale development. Value not stated. [481]

The BlackChamber Group #

Jan 15, 2025 · Financing · Northern Virginia, VA · 740 MW · $1.2B · with JLL Capital Markets (financing arranger; individual lenders undisclosed)

JLL Capital Markets announced it arranged over $1.2 billion in construction financing throughout 2024 on behalf of BlackChamber to develop four hyperscale powered-shell campuses in Northern Virginia totaling over 740MW. Note: announcement made by JLL, not the borrower. [482]

Applied Digital #

Jan 14, 2025 · Financing · Ellendale, ND · 400 MW · $5B · with Macquarie Asset Management

Applied Digital agreed a partnership with Macquarie Asset Management for funding of up to $5 billion for HPC/data center growth, tied to the 400MW Ellendale, ND campus (site has 2GW+ potential). Note: $900M committed initially + $4.1B right of first refusal; value recorded as up-to $5B. [483][484]

Digital Realty #

Jan 14, 2025 · Financing · multiple

Digital Realty priced 850 million euros of guaranteed notes due 2035 to fund European data-center buildout. value_usd is null because the deal was stated in euros. [485]

EdgeConneX #

Jan 13, 2025 · New build · Osaka-Kyoto, Japan · 140 MW · with Kagoya Asset Management (land lease partner)

EdgeConneX announced its entry into the Japanese market via a land lease in the greater Osaka-Kyoto area (with Kagoya Asset Management, incl. Tatara R&D), targeting more than 140MW ready-for-service in 2027. Note: MW stated as 'more than 140MW'; recorded as 140. [486][487]

Castleforge (with Galaxy Data Centers) #

Jan 8, 2025 · Acquisition · Redhill, UK · 26 MW · with Redhill Data Centre (seller undisclosed)

Real estate investor Castleforge, in partnership with operator Galaxy Data Centers, acquired the Redhill Data Centre campus near London (11,800 sqm, three buildings); Castleforge's first data center investment, financed by ICG Real Estate. [488][489][490]

Note: Development value reported as over £100M; purchase price undisclosed. 26MVA power.

Amazon Web Services #

Jan 7, 2025 · New build · Butts County, GA · $11B

AWS announced at least $11 billion investment in Georgia for AI/cloud infrastructure buildout. MW not stated. [491][492]

Microsoft #

Jan 7, 2025 · Expansion · India · $3B

Microsoft announced $3 billion investment over two years in India cloud and AI infrastructure, covering expansion of existing data center footprint. No site/MW stated. [493]

Digital Edge (DC Platform) #

Jan 6, 2025 · Financing · Singapore · $1.6B

Digital Edge raised $1.6 billion ($640M equity + $1B debt) to fund AI-driven data center expansion across Asia. Singapore-based operator. [494]

AirTrunk #

Jan 1, 2025 · Financing · Johor Bahru, Malaysia · 270 MW · $2.3B · with 30 local and international institutions (BNP Paribas, HSBC, MUFG among coordinators); IFC $175M

AirTrunk secured $2.3 billion in green financing for its JHB2 campus in Johor Bahru, Malaysia (270 MW+ across a 520-hectare site), including a $175 million IFC investment. Announced in 2025; exact date not verified, so the date is a placeholder. [495]

DayOne (GDS Holdings affiliate) #

Jan 1, 2025 · Financing · Johor, Malaysia · 750 MW · with Asian bank consortium

GDS's international unit DayOne secured a RM15 billion (~$3.5 billion) multi-currency green financing deal to fund its Malaysian data-center build-out (750 MW committed power pipeline). Announced in 2025; exact date not verified, so the date is a placeholder. value_usd is null because the deal was stated in Malaysian ringgit. [496]

Equinix #

Jan 1, 2025 · Financing · Singapore

Equinix issued a S$650 million green bond due 2032. Announced in 2025; exact date not verified, so the date is a placeholder. value_usd is null because the deal was stated in Singapore dollars. [259]
